# Ease Language Reference (1-Page LLM Guide)

Ease is a small, strict, bracket-free language implemented in Go.
Every construct has **one canonical form** and **zero silent fallbacks**.

## 1. Core Invariants
- **No `bool`, no `true`/`false` literals, no storable conditions**: Keep conditions (`x > 0`, `a is b`, `and`, `or`, `not`) inside `check` and `test` (there is no `if` keyword). Conditions cannot be stored, printed, passed, or returned (`ok = 3 > 2` or `say 3 > 2` raises `TypeError: Conditions cannot be stored or printed...`). Return or store outcomes via explicit `def` union types/records (`def status = "OK" | "FAILED"`, `def decision` with `answer = "yes" | "no"`).
- **Two `check` forms & arrow semantics (`->`)**: Use single-line `check <cond> -> <expr_or_stmt>` for flat guards/loop filters, and block `check ... end` for exhaustive union matches and `else` fallbacks (bare `check` without `->` or `else` is a parse error; abort explicitly with `check <cond> -> fail "..."`). Inside a `to` function, `-> <value>` returns immediately from the whole function (even out of `loop`), while `-> <stmt>` (`say`, assignment) executes and continues. Inside `loop`, `check <cond> -> end` exits only the innermost `loop`. At top level, `check <cond> -> <value>` is an error (`Cannot return a value from 'check' at top level; use 'say' or 'fail' instead.`).
- **Scoping & unified `loop` (`it`, `it.index`, `xs.(expr)`)**: Top-level variables and `def` constants are readable inside `to` functions, but **globals are read-only inside functions** ("Assigned-in-Function = Local": assignments create/update locals without mutating globals; reading a global before a local assignment of the same name fails with `Cannot modify global '...' inside a function...`). Function parameters are immutable. `check` (`->` and `else`) and `loop` are block-scoped. There is only `loop <list|range> ... end` (no `for`, `repeat`, `in`, or named loop vars): `it` holds the element and `it.index` holds the 0-based index (`def` fields cannot be named `index`). Computed list indexing uses `xs.(expr)` (e.g. `seq.(it.index - 1)`).
- **Arity-based prefix calls (`def` / `to`, no `do`)**: `def` = noun blueprint (`def ErrorMessage`), `to` = English infinitive action verb (`to process_response res` — avoid nouns/questions like `to user_data` or `to can_ship`). Call functions directly by name (`process_response res`, `sum_squares range 1 5`, `add (1 + 2) 3`) — `do` was removed. Every `to`/built-in function has a fixed arity collected in a two-pass parser; function/built-in names cannot collide with variable, constant, or parameter names.
- **No commas in function signatures or calls**: Declare `to add a b ... end` and call `add 2 3`. Commas are only for `list 10, 25, 40` and single-line `with` updates.
- **No `==`, `!=`, `is-not` (asymmetric `is` & union typo protection)**: `<value> is <type>` checks type/union membership (`a is user`, `"OK" is status`, `x is number`), `<value> is <value>` checks structural value equality (`x is 5`, `a is b`). **Types are forbidden on the left side of `is`**: `user is a` or `user is user` raises `TypeError`. Comparing a union-typed value against an invalid string literal (e.g., `d.answer is "yse"` for `"yes" | "no"`) raises `TypeError` (`"yse" is not a value of decision.answer ("yes" | "no")`). Nested `def` record defaults (e.g. `a = pt`) are instantiated as concrete values immediately.
- **Atomic negative literals**: `-2` (no space) is a negative number literal (`f -2`). `a - 2` (space after `-`) is subtraction (`count - 2`). Compound arguments use parentheses (`fib (n - 1)`).
- **Built-in runtime types**: `number`, `text`, `list`, `nothing` (plus `def` records and unions).
- **Raw text vs interpolated text**: `'...'` reads 1:1 with zero `{...}` interpolation and zero backslash escapes (ideal for JSON literals). `"..."` supports `{expr}` interpolation strictly for atomic `text`/`number` values (interpolating a `def` record or `list` raises `TypeError`).
- **Orthogonal Union Types (`def U = A | B | ...`)**:
  - **4 building blocks**: literals (`"OK"`, `404`), base types (`text`, `number`), record blueprints (`ErrorMessage`), and other named unions (automatically flattened: `def outcome = status | ErrorMessage`). Unions can also be used as record field types (`res = outcome`) and typed lists (`list as outcome`).
  - **3 compile-time guardrails**: (1) No redundant literals with `text`/`number` (`'OK' is already covered by 'text'`), (2) No duplicates (`"OK" | "OK"`, `User | User`, or across flattening), (3) Records in the same union (`Admin | Guest`) must differ in at least one mandatory field name, field type, or disjoint inline union constraint so `raw_map as <union>` stays unambiguous.
  - **Type Narrowing & Exhaustiveness in `check`**: Inside `res is ErrorMessage -> ...` (and after an early exit `check res is not ErrorMessage -> ...`), `res` narrows to `ErrorMessage` and allows `res.code` / `res.message`; accessing record fields before narrowing raises a static `TypeError`. A `check ... end` dispatch on a closed union must cover every variant or specify an explicit fallback (`else -> ...` or a post-`end` expression); otherwise compile fails with `Non-exhaustive check on '<union>' (Missing case: ...)`.
- **Explicit JSON + strict `as` contracts (no implicit JSON magic)**:
  - `decode_json raw` parses JSON text -> `map`/`list`/primitives (JSON `true`/`false` become `"true"` / `"false"` text; fails immediately on empty or invalid JSON). `encode_json val` serializes structured data -> JSON text (`def` record fields with `"true" | "false"` union schema serialize back as unquoted JSON booleans `true`/`false`; regular `text` fields and free maps stay JSON strings).
  - `as text` works only on atomic values (`text`, `number`) — records/lists raise `TypeError`.
  - `<map_or_record> as <def_record_or_union>` validates structured data (raw `text` directly -> `TypeError`). **All `def` fields are mandatory** (`Missing field '<type>.<field>'`); extra keys are tolerated.
  - Defaults belong exclusively to `<def> with ...` (`hero = user with id = 1`).

## 2. Syntax Cheat Sheet
```ease
import network

def pi = 3.14
def status = "OK" | "FAILED"

def ErrorMessage
    code    = 500
    message = "Unknown error"
end

def outcome = status | ErrorMessage

def user
    id   = 0
    name = "Guest"
    role = "guest" | "admin"
end

to process_response res
    check
        res is "OK"         -> "Processed successfully"
        res is "FAILED"     -> "Unknown failure"
        res is ErrorMessage -> "Error {res.code}: {res.message}"
    end
end

to log_only_success res
    check
        res is "OK" -> "Succeeded"
        else        -> "Something else happened"
    end
end

to greet u
    check
        u is not user        -> "Invalid user"
        u.role is "admin"    -> "Admin: {u.name}"
    end
    "Hello {u.name}"
end

to add a b
    a + b
end

# Records, unions, lists, loops, explicit JSON decode + strict contract validation
ada = user with id = 1, name = "Aria", role = "admin"
nums = list 10, 20, 30
first = nums.0
idx = 1
second = nums.(idx)
empty = list as number

loop range 1 3
    check it > 2 -> end
    say "{it.index}: {add it 10}"
end

# `loop xs ... end` binds only `it` and `it.index` (always access record fields via `it.<field>`)
users = list as user with
    id = 1, name = "Aria"
end
loop users
    say "#{it.index} {it.id}: {it.name}"
end

raw_map = decode_json '{"id": 7, "name": "Guest", "role": "admin"}'
parsed = raw_map as user
encoded = encode_json parsed

raw_err = decode_json '{"code": 503, "message": "Unavailable"}' as outcome

test "example"
    add 2 3 is 5
    greet ada is "Admin: Aria"
    process_response "OK" is "Processed successfully"
    process_response raw_err is "Error 503: Unavailable"
    log_only_success "OK" is "Succeeded"
    log_only_success raw_err is "Something else happened"
    "abc" as number is error
    '{"id": 7, "name": "Guest", "role": "admin"}' as user is error
    (decode_json '{"id": 7, "role": "admin"}') as user ->
        error.type is "TypeError"
        error.message is "Missing field 'user.name'"
    end
    (ada with id = "bad") is error
    (user is ada) is error
end
```

## 3. Built-in Verbs & CLI
- **Data-driven `test` blocks**: `test "label" ... end` supports assignments, `loop` over test cases, direct boolean conditions (`a + b <= 20`), `is` / `is not`, `expr is error` / `expr is not error`, and `expr -> error.type is "..." / error.message is "..." end` blocks. All assertions run as soft asserts with full enclosing block context on failure (`ease test <file> [--verbose]`).
- **Lists, vector arithmetic, `where` filters, batch `with` & aggregations**: Numeric lists support element-wise `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` (matching lengths required; division/modulo by zero aborts) and scalar broadcasting (`prices * 1.19 + shipping`, `100 - discounts`). Filter lists declaratively with `<list> where <cond>` (single-line `orders where it.status is "paid" and it.amount > 50` or multi-line `where ... end` block with AND-combined conditions and union narrowing on `it`); update record lists uniformly via `cloud with x = it.x + it.vx` (both `where` and batch `with` bind `it` and `it.index`, never implicit fields). Use `append xs item_or_list` to append elements or combine lists (`+` on non-numeric lists raises `TypeError`). Use `sum xs`, `avg xs`, and `sort xs` (returns sorted copy of `number`/`text` lists) for data processing.
- **Verbs**: `say expr`, `ask prompt`, `count xs`, `str val`, `num val`, `type val`, `range start end`, `append xs item_or_list`, `sum xs`, `avg xs`, `sort xs`, `abs n`, `min a b`, `max a b`, `fields rec`, `decode_json txt`, `encode_json val`, `fail msg`
- **Std modules**: `import network` (`network`, `fetch client path`, `send client path payload`), `import screen` (`screen`, `circle`, `box`, `scene`, `frame_state`, `present win current_scene`)
- **CLI**: `ease run <file> [--check] [--trace]`, `ease test <file> [--verbose] [--trace]`, `ease build <file> [-o out]`, `ease ast <file>`, `ease tokens <file>`, `ease lsp`
